meta.title: The A Form: The Barre You Already Own
meta.summary: The A form's grip is x 1 5 1 3 5 — its top note is the fifth, not the root, and exactly one string decides whether the whole chord is major.

spans.text: This is the barre chord almost everyone already owns before they've ever heard the word CAGED. So the point of this lesson isn't the grip — your hand has that. The point is what's inside it, which nobody ever told you.

Start with why it holds whole at all. Barre at fret 3, and nothing in the grip reaches further than fret 5 — two frets past the barre, at most. The C form asked for three frets past the barre and a root stranded out at the far end. The A form never asks for more than two, on any string, and that's the whole difference between a barre chord you fight and one you don't.

It matters whenever that string rings alone or carries a line: what's sounding is a fifth, not the note the chord is named after. The two

That's as far as this pathway takes minor chords; the forms that build on it are a different pathway, but the one finger that decides it is worth knowing cold.
